chunks: 3. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Hamzah ibn Muhammad, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)
asking him about the body and the image/appearance, so he (peace be upon him) wrote to me: Glory to the One who has nothing like Him, no body and no image.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Kadhim say about whether Allah has a body or form?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, this hadith from Imam al-Kadhim (AS) serves as a foundational proof for the Shia doctrine of divine incorporeality (*tanzih*), refuting anthropomorphic views by asserting Allah's absolute transcendence. The Imam’s concise response, 'Subhan man laysa ka-mithlihi shay’' (Glory to Him who is not like anything), directly links the negation of physical form (*jism*) and visible image (*surah*) to the Quranic attribute of incomparability, establishing that God’s essence is beyond human sensory perception and spatial limitations.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 3. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan Al-Saffar, on the authority of Sahl ibn Ziyad, on the authority of Hamzah ibn Muhammad saying, "I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Kadhim (AS)
asking him about the body and the appearance of Allah; therefore, he (AS) wrote to me: “Glory to the One who has nothing like Him, and who has no body and no image.”
